description: The game's fonts are created with lfQuality 0 (DEFAULT_QUALITY: the recordings' CreateFontIndirectA arguments, quality column 0 in port/corpus/widths/*.widths.json). On this host (SPI_GETFONTSMOOTHING 1, SPI_GETFONTSMOOTHINGTYPE 2 = ClearType, contrast 1200, orientation 1 = RGB) the DEFAULT_QUALITY raster equals the CLEARTYPE_QUALITY raster on all 45 sweep texts and differs from NONANTIALIASED_QUALITY on 42 and ANTIALIASED_QUALITY on 42 (log/roadmap/S5/2_facts.log). That a host with font smoothing off or set to standard (greyscale) gives the NONANTIALIASED / ANTIALIASED raster instead is the documented meaning of DEFAULT_QUALITY, not measured: no system setting was changed.
path to resolution: Run `labels.py facts` and `labels.py reference` in a user session (or VM) where smoothing is off and where it is standard, and record the digests per setting.

description: The reference digests (port/corpus/labels/reference.json) are this host's ClearType raster, which reads the session's ClearType parameters (contrast 1200, RGB orientation; facts.json `host`). A host with another contrast or orientation is expected to give other digests; not measured for the same reason as U-1510. A FreeType provider (S5.3) that targets these digests targets ClearType at these parameters.
path to resolution: Record the reference under a second contrast value in a separate session; S5.3 decides which raster the port's provider reproduces.

description: drawCenteredText2 and drawTextSurface set shadow colour 1 with offset (0, 1) (setQuad(colour, 1, 0, 1), c3dq.cpp), and the run drawer resolves a non-direct shadow colour through the palette (SetRunColour, c3et.cpp). The RGB of palette index 1 at those calls is not determined in this step: the corpus's `shadow` configuration draws the shadow in 0x0000 as a stand-in. A provider equal on single transparent draws is equal on the two-draw sequence whatever that colour is, so the stand-in does not weaken the comparison, but the corpus does not show the game's shadow colour.
path to resolution: Read palette index 1 of the surfaces those callers draw on (the display palette at the call, from a recording or the gfx backend's palette) and add it to the shadow configuration.

description: The colour scan (log/roadmap/S5/2_colours.py over the function ranges of re/functions_ghidra.tsv) reads the colour word of 414 text call sites from immediate pushes; 125 sites pass the colour in a register or from memory and their words are not in the corpus's colour list (21 direct words from the 289 others). The `base` and `inverse` configurations cover the two most common words (0x80007fff, 0x80000000) for every entry.
path to resolution: Resolve the register / memory colours from the C3 / C4 notes of the callers or from a recording of setQuad's first argument.

description: Controls 1 (last glyph one pixel right) and 3 (last character dropped) leave unchanged the jobs whose last byte draws no ink (a trailing space, a lone space): 2,184 of 15,960 corpus jobs read equal under each (13,776 RED). They are equivalent mutants on those jobs only; the other jobs and every checkpoint read them RED.
path to resolution: none needed; recorded so a future count of RED jobs is not read as a gap
